text:
experiment: noul-retention-v2
question: is Jev's Noul P(retains) a better forecast of the sealed outcome than the permuted Choice P(retains), and better than a coin?
outcome: rule native-retention-6h-v1 (ops/journal/resolution-rule.json), unchanged
journal: ops/journal/jev-local.jsonl (local Jev runs only; no model key on GitHub)
arms, one journal action each, never pooled:
  wallet_promotion@noul      Jev Noul probability of the statement below, one request, one wallet
  wallet_promotion@permuted  the permutation-brier-v1 arm, unchanged, from the same hunt and wallet
  wallet_promotion@constant  0.5, fixed
noul statement, verbatim: "Six hours after the transfer described, the sending wallet's native PLS balance is at least what it was at the time of the transfer."
noul request: SEPARATE from the v1 request, so v1's sealed request is unchanged; same state
egress: value_pls, balance_pls, fraction_sent only; the address is not sent
recording: noul and constant are recorded only when the v1 pair AND the noul call both succeed; a failed call records neither
pairing: wallets with all three arms resolved; only wallets hunted after this seal have a noul arm
metric: Brier per arm over the paired wallets
minimum: 97 paired resolved wallets; below that the verdict is UNDERPOWERED, not a result
prediction: Brier(noul) <= Brier(permuted) - 0.02 AND Brier(noul) < Brier(constant)
verdict: HELD if the prediction holds at the minimum, else FALSIFIED
falsifier consequence: if noul does not beat constant, no Jev arm gets promotion weight on these three features
pre-seal observation (exploratory, not a result; v1 still below its minimum): 83 v1 pairs, Brier single 0.350, permuted 0.312, both worse than 0.25; mean P(retains) 0.22/0.29 vs 58% retained
external evidence: jev-does-not-play-dice (MIT) -- Choice sharpens probabilities; Noul closer to stated/true probabilities
out of scope: encoded-state arm (separate id); batching wallets per request
